definition: An input deliberately crafted, often with small, imperceptible perturbations, to cause a machine learning model to make an incorrect prediction.
details: Adversarial examples reveal that models can be highly sensitive to inputs that look nearly identical to humans but are perceived very differently by the model, raising robustness and security concerns.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. In plain words: An input deliberately crafted, often with small, imperceptible perturbations, to cause a machine learning model to make an incorrect prediction. Here is how it actually plays out: Adversarial examples reveal that models can be highly sensitive to inputs that look nearly identical to humans but are perceived very differently by the model, raising robustness and security concerns. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Adversarial Example.
